Claim 31 (Currently amended): A system for treating obesity, the system comprising: a gastric space filler comprising a first balloon connected to a second balloon by a conduit, wherein the gastric space filler is configured to occupy a substantial volume of a gastric cavity in the human patient in an inflated state; and an instrument throughput channel extending through the conduit, wherein the instrument throughput channel is configured to receive instruments and is integrated within the conduit structure.

Claim 32 (Currently amended): The system of claim 31 wherein the conduit comprises a first lumen in fluid communication with the first balloon, a second lumen in fluid communication with the second balloon, and a third lumen defining the instrument throughput channel, the third lumen extending fully along the length of the conduit.

Claim 33 (Currently amended): The system of claim 31 wherein the conduit has an axial length, and wherein the instrument throughput channel extends along the entirety of the axial length of the conduit.

Claim 34 (Currently amended): The system of claim 31 wherein the gastric space filler further comprises a coupling mechanism configured to facilitate engagement with a retrieval device for removal of the gastric space filler from the gastric cavity; the retrieval device being configured for operation through the esophagus.

Claim 35 (Currently amended): The system of claim 31 wherein the first and second balloons are made from at least one of the following: silicone, latex, polyethylene, polyurethane, and nylon, with materials selected based on their biocompatibility and durability.

Claim 36 (Currently amended): The system of claim 31 wherein the conduit comprises an inter-balloon section spacing the first balloon apart from the second balloon, and wherein the inter-balloon section has a length of about 10-40 mm, specifically configured for optimal spacing during operation. 

Claim 41 (Currently amended): The system of claim 31, further comprising a delivery catheter configured to deliver the gastric space filler to the gastric cavity via an esophagus of the patient, wherein the delivery catheter is configured to receive the gastric space filler in a collapsed state suitable for passage through anatomical structures. 

Claim 42 (Currently amended): A gastric space filler system, comprising: a conduit having a first end and a second end opposite the first end, wherein the first end is operably coupled to a first balloon and the second end is operably coupled to a second balloon; a first lumen through the conduit, wherein the lumen is configured for fluid infusion into the first balloon; a second lumen through the conduit, wherein the second lumen is configured for fluid infusion into the second balloon; and a third lumen extending through the conduit, wherein the third lumen is configured for instrument throughput, extending fully from the first to the second end. 

Claim 43 (Currently amended): The gastric space filler system of claim 42 wherein: the first lumen extends from the first end of the conduit to the first balloon; and the second lumen extends from the first end of the conduit to the second balloon, allowing for independent operation of inflation.

Claim 44 (Currently amended): The gastric space filler system of claim 42 wherein the third lumen extends from the first end of the conduit to a second end of the conduit, allowing for efficient access for instruments.

Claim 45 (Currently amended): The gastric space filler system of claim 42, further comprising a coupling mechanism at the first end of the conduit, wherein the coupling mechanism is configured for instrument throughput into the third lumen and configured to couple to a delivery catheter and/or a filling tube.

Claim 46 (Currently amended): The gastric space filler system of claim 42 wherein the gastric space filler system is configured for delivery through an esophagus of a patient to a stomach of the patient utilizing minimally invasive techniques.

Claim 47 (Currently amended): The gastric space filler system of claim 42 wherein the conduit is configured for attachment to a delivery catheter, and wherein the third lumen of the conduit is configured to receive an instrument passed through the delivery catheter for versatile application.
